name: Graveyard of Kings
note: Archaeological site: about 20 stone tombs on Sisilo hill, Rotuma (Wikivoyage See). No article under this title.

name: Solroroa Bluff
note: Hilltop hiking viewpoint with spectacular views over Rotuma (Wikivoyage Do). Walk, not a built attraction.

name: Mount Suelhof
note: Hill: highest point on Rotuma (256 m), near the island centre, hiking and views (Wikivoyage Do). No article under this title.

name: Manfiri Volcanic Vent
note: Volcanic vent about 25 m deep between Losa beach and Solroroa Bluff, on the hiking route (Wikivoyage Do). One search snippet spells it Mamfiri.

name: Losa Beach
note: Beach: one of the best beaches on Rotuma, west of Solroroa Bluff (Wikivoyage Do). Village of Losa is in Ituʻtiʻu district.

name: Vai'oa Beach
note: Beach: one of the best beaches on Rotuma, west of Solroroa Bluff (Wikivoyage Do). No article.

name: Oinafa Beach
note: Beach: one of the best beaches on Rotuma, in the Oinafa district on the east (Wikivoyage Do). Wiki title is the district article, so views are 0. No beach point found: the district article point is not used.

name: Joro Beach
note: Beach and picnic area on the main island (Wikivoyage Do). No article.

name: Lulu Beach
note: Beach and picnic area on the main island (Wikivoyage Do). No article.

name: 'Ana-te-Fapufa Cave
note: Cave: 'Fapufa cave', a popular picnic and visit stop on the main island (Wikivoyage Do). Fapufa is a village in Ituʻtiʻu.

name: Agaha Islet
note: Islet: about 1.2 km off the southeast coast, named by Wikivoyage as an ideal picnic spot. Spelled ʻAgaha in Wikipedia-style sources.

name: Solkope
note: Islet: about 75 m offshore, named by Wikivoyage as an ideal picnic spot. Reachable from the main island's reef.

name: Hatana
note: Islet in the Rotuma group, north-west of Rotuma Island: seabird colony of national significance. Wikipedia says access is restricted (sacred or taboo status, owned by Losa village). Not a visitor stop.

name: Hafliua Islet
note: Islet in the Rotuma group west of the main island: nationally significant seabird colony. Spelled Hofliua in the brief; no visitor source found for access.

name: Solnohu
note: Islet off the southern coast of Faguta, the southernmost point of the Rotuma group: local turtle myth (Sol Onau) and turtle feeding beach nearby. No visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Mofmanu Beach
note: Beach: the popular main beach beside Motusa village on the isthmus, one of the island's longest white sand beaches (Wikipedia). No article; wiki title is the village. No OSM feature found; the village point is not used for the beach.

name: Motusa
note: Village (group of villages) on the low isthmus, the site of the island's main beach. A village, not a stop in itself: the beach is the draw.

name: Ahau
note: Village: the capital and seat of the Council of Rotuma (meeting house), and the transport arrival point (Wikivoyage Get in). No visitor draw named.

name: Ituʻtiʻu
note: District: one of Rotuma's seven districts (capital district), covering Ahau, Motusa and Hapmak. Not a visitor stop itself; a Wikipedia district article.

name: Hapmak
note: Village in Ituʻtiʻu district, between Motusa and Losa on the western side of the isthmus. No visitor draw found.

name: Maftoa
note: Village on the western peninsula (Ituʻmuta district), with Lopo. No visitor draw found.

name: Hapmafau Bay
note: Bay in the south of the isthmus: large coral reef with boat passages (Wikipedia). Bay with reef and boat access, not a named visitor stop.

name: Maka Bay
note: Bay north of the isthmus, with a large coral reef and boat passages (Wikipedia). Not a named visitor stop.

name: Satarua Peak
note: Hill: 166 m, near the eastern end of Rotuma (Wikipedia). Named as a height only, not as a place to go.

name: Stonebridge (Rotuma)
note: Natural rock bridge (stone bridge) on Rotuma, a motorbike-ride stop named in a Fiji Sun article. Found in a search snippet, not fetched.
